newsitem.title: LATVIA: PORT TURNOVER GAINS IN FIRST FIVE MONTHS-REPORT.
newsitem.headline: PORT TURNOVER GAINS IN FIRST FIVE MONTHS-REPORT.

text.p: The turnover of Latvia's ports rose by 2.5 million tonnes in the first five months of 1997 from the same period last year to 20.9 million tonnes, newspaper Dienas Bizness on Monday quoted the transport ministry as saying.
"So our aim of 50 million tonnes this year is real," the newspaper quoted transport ministry transit department head Zigmars Priede as saying.

He told the newspaper that the rise in transit cargo was helped by increased tariffs for rail transport in Lithuania which meant business was diverted to Latvia. The tough winter conditions at Russian ports also helped Latvia's ports.
In the first five months, the largest port of Ventspils transported mainly oil products at 12.04 million tonnes, a rise from 11.49 million tonnes, in the first five months.
Riga and Liepaja ports transported mostly timber products at 1.09 million tonnes in Riga versus 560,000 tonnes and 270,000 tonnes in Liepaja versus 250,000 tonnes.
